issues.legal_issue: An interim rent-payment order does not merge into a later order addressing arrears after trial when the earlier order governed a distinct period and the tenant failed to comply with it.
material_facts: The Rent Controller ordered the tenant to pay or deposit monthly rent from 1 October 2004 onward, while leaving the dispute over rent arrears for the earlier period unresolved.
After trial, the Rent Controller found that the tenant had not proved payment of the earlier arrears and had also failed to pay rent as directed by the interim order.
A later order directed payment of the arrears and modified the interim order; the tenant argued that the later order caused the interim order to merge into it.
issues.conclusion: The interim order did not merge into the later order, and its non-compliance remained relevant to the tenant’s entitlement to protection from eviction.
issues.legal_principle: The orders addressed distinct periods: the interim order required monthly rent payments while leaving the earlier arrears dispute open, and the later order followed the finding at trial that the arrears had not been paid. The Court therefore rejected the merger argument under the framework of Sections 14(1)(a), 14(2), and 15(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.

rule.if: rent_default_eviction_proceeding and earlier_order_governed_distinct_period and earlier_order_left_arrears_unresolved and tenant_failed_to_comply_with_earlier_order

predicates.rent_default_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding alleging that a tenant had failed to pay rent.
predicates.earlier_order_governed_distinct_period: The rent-payment order addressed a period distinct from the arrears later considered after trial.
predicates.earlier_order_left_arrears_unresolved: The court left the dispute about the earlier rent arrears undecided when it made the rent-payment order.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_comply_with_earlier_ord: The tenant did not make the rent payments required by the earlier order.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding involves an earlier rent-payment order for a distinct period, that order left arrears unresolved, and the tenant failed to comply with it, the earlier order does not merge into a later order.

issues.legal_issue: A court may condone delay in depositing rent only when the defaulting tenant pleads justifiable reasons showing that circumstances beyond the tenant’s control prevented timely compliance; unexplained willful default does not warrant condonation.
material_facts: The tenant was directed to pay or deposit monthly rent during the proceeding but failed to do so regularly, and the Nazir’s report showed substantial delays.
The tenant had maintained that he had paid the arrears, but the Rent Controller found that he had not proved payment or tender of rent after the demand notice.
The tenant gave no explanation for the delays in depositing rent, and the Rent Controller denied him the benefit of protection from eviction.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not entitled to condonation of the delays or to the benefit of Section 14(2), and the eviction order was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: In Hem Chand etc. etc. v. The Delhi Cloth & General Mills Co. Ltd. and Anr. etc. etc., the Court had held that there was no discretion to extend time for payment under Section 15(1). Relying on Shyamcharan Sharma v. Dharamdas and Ram Murti v. Bhola Nath and Anr., the Court recognized that the Rent Controller may condone default in payment or deposit of future rent. That discretion applies where the tenant seeks condonation and pleads justifiable reasons showing that circumstances beyond the tenant’s control prevented compliance. Under Sections 14(2) and 15(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, compliance with the rent-payment order is required for protection from eviction on the ground of non-payment.

rule.if: rent_default_eviction_proceeding and tenant_delayed_required_rent_deposits and tenant_willfully_defaulted and tenant_offered_no_justifiable_explanation

predicates.rent_default_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding on the ground that a tenant had failed to pay rent.
predicates.tenant_delayed_required_rent_deposits: The tenant deposited rent later than the times required by the court’s rent-payment order.
predicates.tenant_willfully_defaulted: The tenant failed to make the required rent payments despite being ordered to do so.
predicates.tenant_offered_no_justifiable_explanatio: The tenant did not provide a justifiable reason showing that circumstances beyond the tenant’s control prevented timely payment.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a rent-default eviction proceeding delays required rent deposits, willfully defaults, and provides no justifiable explanation, condonation and protection from eviction are denied.
